summary: Florida is permissive to keep a pet roof rat, with one paid-sale catch, now confirmed directly by FWC. FWC decides 'domestic vs. wild' by SPECIES, not by how tame an individual is, so roof/black rats count as 'wild rats' even when captive-bred for generations. The upshot (FWC Captive Wildlife, written reply 2026-06-08): KEEPING one as a pet needs NO license, and GIVING one away (any transfer with no money) needs NO license, all rats are exempt from personal-possession licensing. But SELLING one (any transfer for money) requires a Class III 'Exhibition or Public Sale' (ESC) license. Importing a roof rat into Florida needs a free 45-day FWC Wildlife Importation Permit plus a veterinary health certificate. Never release a nonnative.
agency_confirmations: FWC Captive Wildlife Office (written reply, 2026-06-08): FWC determines whether an animal is domestic or wild by the SPECIES, not by an individual's tameness, so black/roof rats are treated as wild rats even when captive-bred. KEEPING one as a pet requires NO license (all rats, wild or domestic, are exempt from personal-possession licensing), and GIVING one away with no money changing hands requires NO license. SELLING one (any transfer for payment) requires a Class III 'Exhibition or Public Sale' (ESC) license.
FDACS Division of Animal Industry (written guidance, 2020): importing animals into Florida requires a veterinary health certificate (OCVI) issued within 30 days; reportable diseases must be reported.

keep.why: FWC confirmed in writing (2026-06-08) that ALL rats, wild or domestic, are exempt from personal-possession licensing, so keeping a captive-bred roof rat as a pet needs no FWC license. (Consistent with F.A.C. 68A-6.003(14)(d), which exempts 'Rats and mice' for personal use, and with roof rats not being on FWC's Prohibited Nonnative Species list.)
keep.governing_law: F.A.C. 68A-6.003(14)(d) (personal-use exemption); FWC Captive Wildlife written confirmation 2026-06-08; FWC Prohibited Nonnative Species List (not listed).

breed.why: Breeding for personal use, keeping the offspring as your own pets or giving them away free, requires no FWC license (all rats are exempt from personal-possession licensing). There is no separate FWC 'breeding permit.' Note: the moment you SELL offspring (transfer for money), the selling rule below applies (a Class III ESC license).
breed.governing_law: F.A.C. 68A-6.003(14)(d) (personal use); FWC written confirmation 2026-06-08; commercial sale → 68A-6.004 (Class III).

sell_give.why: RESOLVED by FWC's written reply (2026-06-08): because FWC treats roof rats as WILDLIFE by species (not by tameness), SELLING one, any transfer where money changes hands, requires a Class III 'Exhibition or Public Sale' (ESC) license. GIVING one away with no payment requires NO license (all rats are exempt from personal-possession licensing). This supersedes the brief 2020 verbal 'no license to sell' guidance, which didn't account for the species-based doctrine.
sell_give.governing_law: FWC Captive Wildlife written confirmation 2026-06-08; F.A.C. 68A-6.004 (Class III 'Exhibition or Public Sale' license, $50/yr); 68A-6.003(12).

transport.why: Moving an exempt personal pet within Florida needs no permit. IMPORTING a roof rat into Florida (it is non-native wildlife) requires a FREE FWC Wildlife Importation Permit (CWL), valid 45 days (applicant must be 16+); and FDACS requires a veterinary health certificate (OCVI) for animals entering the state. It is illegal to release any nonnative species.
transport.governing_law: FWC Wildlife Importation (CWL); Fla. Admin. Code ch. 5C-3 / FDACS (OCVI); FWC nonnative-species no-release.

restrictions.summary: To SELL roof rats (any transfer for money), you need a Class III 'License to Possess Wildlife for Exhibition or Public Sale' (ESC), $50/yr, confirmed required by FWC (2026-06-08) because roof rats are wildlife by species. GIVING them away free needs no license. No experience hours, but a disaster plan + inventory/source recordkeeping are required for the ESC.
steps: If you'll sell for money: apply for the Class III Exhibition/Public Sale (ESC) license and file a disaster plan
If only giving away free: nothing required
restrictions.fees: $50/yr (Class III ESC) to sell; $0 to give away

restrictions.summary: To bring a roof rat INTO Florida, get a free FWC Wildlife Importation Permit (CWL), valid 45 days (applicant must be 16+), plus a veterinary health certificate (OCVI) issued within 30 days. Applies to private and commercial moves alike.
steps: Apply for the FWC Wildlife Importation Permit (CWL) before crossing into Florida
Carry a veterinary health certificate (OCVI) issued within 30 days
restrictions.fees: No cost (CWL); veterinary fee for the OCVI

restrictions.summary: It is illegal to release any nonnative species, including roof rats, into the wild in Florida. Keep them contained and rehome responsibly; never release. Local city/county ordinances may also limit exotic-pet keeping or large breeding operations.
restrictions.where_to_file: Your county animal services / municipal code enforcement

inquiry_focus: RESOLVED 2026-06-08 by FWC Captive Wildlife: keeping/giving-away need no license; selling for money needs a Class III ESC license (roof rats are wildlife by species). No open question remains for FWC; transport/import details verified separately.
